source.title: Studying How to Efficiently and Effectively Guide Models with Explanations
source.authors: Sukrut Rao; Moritz D Boehle; Amin Parchami-Araghi; B. Schiele

record.file_problem: Supplied full paper text and supplement; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether explanation guidance changes classification performance and generalization under distribution shifts, a related setting for the claim, using pretrained image classifiers and attribution guidance.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results concern attribution localization and classification effects of explanation guidance, not random-label memorization, width, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Rows below cover classification results relevant to V1 and V5's broad natural-label generalization topic; localization-only comparisons and reported hyperparameter selection values are not rows. The Waterbirds results test distribution-shift behavior, which the claim explicitly separates from ordinary same-distribution generalization, so they are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates explanation guidance, attribution localization, and classification under distribution shifts. None of its results tests the specific relationships in V1–V8. Natural-label classification performance alone does not test V1, and using Adam or a fixed batch size does not test V4 or V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. Bounding-box explanation guidance improves attribution localization and can improve classification for some models, especially under strong spurious correlations and distribution shifts. On VOC and COCO, the authors generally observe a trade-off between localization and classification performance. Energy loss favors EPG, object-specific attribution, and robustness to coarse annotations; L1 favors IoU.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes ImageNet-pretrained image classifiers using bounding-box explanation guidance on VOC, COCO, and Waterbirds; this is not the random-label memorization/generalization protocol in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Guidance loss, attribution method, model type, guidance layer, dataset, annotation fraction and coarseness, and distribution setting change reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.3 reports X-DNN configurations improving F1 by 1.4 percentage points alongside localization improvements, but describes an overall localization–classification trade-off on VOC and COCO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explanation guidance can improve classification for some pretrained image classifiers, while often trading classification performance for attribution localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports that B-cos Energy guidance with bounding boxes for 1% of Waterbirds training images raises conventional-setting overall accuracy from 68.7% to 71.2% and G3 accuracy from 43.4% to 56.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bounding-box explanation guidance can improve classification under foreground–background distribution shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 5.1–5.4 report that Energy loss provides the best EPG–classification trade-off, whereas L1 generally provides the best IoU–classification trade-off; Energy guidance is more robust to coarse bounding boxes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness and annotation robustness of attribution guidance depend on the localization loss and evaluation metric.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2023
record.problems: Classification outcomes are reported for Pareto-dominant model sets or summarized comparisons in the main experiments, rather than a consistent single baseline metric table; the study does not measure the claim's random-label memorization/generalization relationship. Waterbirds evaluates a distribution shift, outside the claim's stated scope.
record.rows_left_out: Localization metric comparisons (EPG, IoU, on-object EPG), including the many model/loss/layer/dataset configurations in Figs. 5–12 and supplement Figs. B1–B9 and X1–X11, were left out because they do not measure generalization gap as defined by the claim versions. Waterbirds conventional and reversed-setting accuracy results in Table 1 and Table C1 were left out because they test distribution-shift behavior, which the claim excludes.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that recover large-batch performance.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with dataset size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its relationship to generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T3 classification and V1 tested_not_extracted status. Empty result rows are appropriate for V1–V8. Waterbirds results fall outside these versions because they evaluate a different intervention and relationship; the supplied versions do not explicitly exclude all distribution-shift research. The introductory citation to Feldman and Zhang does not test V8.

versions.untested_parts: No natural-label versus random-label training comparison or random-label fit result. Ordinary classification outcomes from explanation-guided training are related but do not test memorization capacity.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparison; Adam is used as a training detail.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch generalization-gap test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
